mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stay below baseline while RESIDENTIAL stays at or above baseline, daytime footfall remains suppressed and retail-and-recreation mobility will stay below its recent 4-week average over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages above its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below baseline for most of the period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharper drop in GROCERY_PHARM relative to the prior weeks signals substitution away from essential trips and weaker local errand circulation, which will pull RETAIL_REC lower within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls 2 points or more below its 4-week median
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM crosses 2 points below its 4-week median.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS rises while TRANSIT falls, leisure demand is being reallocated toward open-air destinations instead of shopping districts, so RETAIL_REC will weaken over the next four weeks.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though PARKS increases and TRANSIT decreases concurrently.

evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is already around -20 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to fall relative to the prior 4-week mean after TRANSIT stays below -20 for two straight weeks.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not drop in the week after WORKPLACES posts two weekly declines while RESIDENTIAL remains near zero.
